newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean private copper mining seen up sharply.
newsitem.headline: Chilean private copper mining seen up sharply.

text.p: Chile's privately-owned mines will produce 1.9 million tonnes of fine copper this year, up 42 percent over 1995, said the National Mining Society, a trade group.

State copper production will rise only three percent, in comparison, to 1.2 million tonnes this year over 1995, including output from state-owned Codelco and Empresa Nacional de Mineria, said the society.
The figures underlined the growth in private mining in Chile at the expense of state mining as a percentage of total production.

"Private mining has continued to show dynamic growth, consolidating our country as the world's leader in copper production as well as advancing the production of other metals like gold, silver and non-metallic substances," said the group in a statement.
The group also said copper exports this year would reach $6.17 billion, out of total mining exports of $7.4 billion.

The group, known by its Spanish acronym SONAMI, said total Chilean copper production should rise to 3.43 million tonnes next year, up 10.6 percent from 1996, and reach 4.7 million tonnes in the year 2000.
Production from private mines alone should rise to 3.2 million tonnes in the year 2000, it said.
